nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Who is responsible for providing individuals with the tools needed to develop good epistemic conduct?
nodes.answer: Institutions have a responsibility to provide individuals with the necessary tools through public education to foster good epistemic conduct.
nodes.paragraph: Relying entirely on information when choos - ing a partner leaves out an essential component of dating choices: intuition. The research presented in the paper Evaluating Intel - ligence and Knowledge in Large Language Models by Francesco Bianchini addresses a different issue. Large language models (LLMs) are generative models of artifi - cial intelligence that are able to produce natural language texts in response to human prompts that are almost indis - tinguishable from human-generated texts. Do LMMs pro - mote or hinder knowledge? What are the potential risks to their users? The first issue discussed concerns the immense proliferation of Al-generated texts on the Internet texts that, because of their artificial nature, are not perceived as a source of knowledge, which could end up pushing indi - viduals to retreat into ignorance. Indeed, at some point, ignorance may be perceived as a refuge in the face of the advancement of these technologies, which mimic human intelligence almost perfectly. A second problem relates to the manipulability of LLMs: these systems answer ques - tions posed by humans and can generate completely ficti - tious content.
